classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a supplied right-triangular base area then substitute the explicitly perpendicular height into the taught pyramid formula. Routine two-formula calculation.

inlines.text: In this exercise, assume all pyramids are right pyramids unless otherwise stated.

spec.description: Triangular pyramid with V vertically above A, C to the right of A and B behind and to the right of C. AB is hidden and dashed. Right-angle marks indicate VA perpendicular to AC and AC perpendicular to BC. Ordinary source blue edges and red hidden edge are reconstructed in black.
spec.mathematics: Right-triangular base ABC has perpendicular sides AC=6 cm and BC=8 cm. Perpendicular pyramid height VA=7.5 cm. Visible faces are VAC and VCB; their common edge VC is solid, and the occluded base edge AB is dashed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and geometric marks are visible; no calculated values.

answer.worked:
The base is right-angled at $C$, and $VA$ is the perpendicular height of the pyramid.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times6\times8\\A&=24\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac13Ah\\V&=\frac13\times24\times7.5\\V&=60\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
